## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

There are tonnes of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the 'plot()' function we used last time) and add on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-build data frame 'cars' to play with plotting:
```{r}
head(cars)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```
Now with ggplot:
First I need to install the package with the 'install.packages()' function
>I do not want to run 'install.packages('ggplot2')' in a quarto document as this will result in me reinstalling the package every time I render the report. 

I can use packages I hae installed by loading them using the library() command, in this case 'library(ggplot2)'

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things:

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (the visuals, denoted 'aes', how the columns of the data map tot he plot)
- the **geom** (how the plot should actually be drawn, eg. points, lines, etc...)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method ='lm') +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="Speed(MPH)",
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title="Silly Plot of Stopping Distances")
```

ggplot may be a little more work to initialize, but is easier to modify to specifications in the long run

##Gene Expression Plot

Read the data from online:

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```
```{r}
ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2) +
  geom_point()
```

>Q. How many genes are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

>Q. How many are upregulated?

```{r}
table(genes$State)
sum(genes$State == "up")
```

>Q. What percentage of genes are downregulated

```{r}
round(100*sum(genes$State == "down")/nrow(genes),4)
```
```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes)+
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col = State)+
  geom_point()+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("blue","gray","red")) +
  labs(x="Control (no drug)",
       y="Drug treated",
       title="Gene expression changes upon drug treatment",
       subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novozymes") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
myplot
```

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2) /
(p3 | p4)
```

```{r}
p4 / (p1 | p2 | p3 )
```

```{r}
myplot +
  facet_wrap(~State)
```

## The GapMinder data

The gapminder dataset is rather famous and has lots of plottable data

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

```{r}
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```


> Q. How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder)+
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent)+
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(~continent)

```


```{r}
ggplot(gapminder)+
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent)+
  geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder)+
  aes(x=lifeExp, y=continent, fill=continent)+
  geom_boxplot()
```
